help.title: MSA Consistency Chart
help.body:
Description
MSA Consistency Chart

Purpose
The MSA Consistency Chart evaluates the stability of a measurement system over time. Unlike the Machine MSA which compares machine readings against a reference standard across multiple parts, the Consistency Chart monitors a single stream of measurements taken repeatedly on the same characteristic over time — assessing whether the measurement system remains consistent and capable across shifts, days, or production runs.
Following the AIAG MSA 4th Edition standard and Donald Wheeler's EMP III methodology, it quantifies measurement system variation relative to both the engineering tolerance (product control) and the historical process standard deviation (process control).

Inputs
Date/Index (required) — a timestamp or sequential index identifying when each measurement was taken; used as the x-axis of the I Chart

Measurements (required) — the repeated measurements of the characteristic over time

Reference value (optional) — the known true or nominal value of the characteristic; when omitted, the mean of all measurements is used as the reference, and bias is reported as zero

Tolerance Range (USL − LSL) (required) — the full engineering tolerance; used to express measurement system error as a percentage of the allowable part variation (%Tolerance)

Target (optional) — the nominal design value; when provided, the Probability of Misclassification plot x-axis displays actual part dimension coordinates (e.g. LSL = 499.5, USL = 500.5) rather than centred coordinates (LSL = −0.5, USL = +0.5)

Historical process standard deviation (optional, strongly recommended) — a known long-run process SD; when supplied the Variation Ratio is expressed as a percentage of true process capability (%Process); when omitted the study measurements' own variation is used and a warning is displayed (%Study)

Gage Name, Date of Study, Study performed by (optional) — metadata for the report header

Output Interpretation
MS Standard Deviation is StDev of all measurements — the total measurement system spread over time.

Bias = mean(measurements) − Reference. A non-zero bias indicates the measurement system has a systematic offset from the reference value.

GRR %Tolerance acceptance meter — the primary AIAG acceptance criterion: below 10% is acceptable, 10–30% is marginal, above 30% is unacceptable.

GRR %Process (or %Study) meter — measurement variation as a fraction of process capability.

Probability of Misclassification — shows Alpha Risk (probability of rejecting a conforming part) and Beta Risk (probability of accepting a non-conforming part) across the characteristic range.

Percent Contribution pie — shows Repeatability share of total variation. Since there is no part-to-part component in a consistency chart, all variation is attributed to the measurement system.

I Chart of measurements (optional) — plots each measurement against its Date/Index with control limits based on the moving range. Points outside the limits signal measurement system instability that should be investigated.

t-test for bias (optional) — tests whether the average measurement is statistically different from the reference value; p < 0.05 indicates significant bias requiring recalibration.
